name: Octagonal ring-cusp ion source
blurb: ORIS, the ion source from my Ph.D.: a filament-driven discharge in an octagonal chamber, ring-cusp magnets, and a two-grid extraction system.

systems.label: Plasma chamber
systems.blurb: Where the gas is ionised: the octagonal discharge chamber between its front and back flanges.

systems.label: Ring-cusp magnets
systems.blurb: Permanent magnets on the walls and back, held by flanges and covers. Their cusp field confines the plasma electrons.

systems.label: Filament & feedthroughs
systems.blurb: The hot filament cathode and the vacuum feedthroughs that carry its current.

systems.label: Extraction grids
systems.blurb: Screen and acceleration grids, set a short gap apart, that pull the ions out as a beam.

systems.label: Insulators & hardware
systems.blurb: Alumina bushes and metal bushes that isolate the grids, and the screws that clamp the stack.

groups.label: Discharge chamber
groups.blurb: Octagonal chamber where the plasma is made.

groups.label: Side cusp magnet
groups.blurb: Permanent magnets around the chamber walls, in a ring-cusp arrangement that confines the plasma.

groups.label: Back cusp magnet
groups.blurb: Close the magnetic cusp field across the back of the chamber.

groups.label: Stepped alumina bush
groups.blurb: Isolate the grids from each other and from the source body.

groups.label: Screen grid
groups.blurb: First extraction electrode, facing the plasma. The aperture array forms the beamlets.

groups.label: Brass spacer
groups.blurb: Sets the gap between the grids.

groups.label: Acceleration grid
groups.blurb: Second extraction electrode. The voltage across the gap extracts and accelerates the ions.

groups.label: Filament
groups.blurb: Hot cathode: emits the electrons that ionise the gas.
